1	# Draft: a section for agent/skills/kvit-ui/SKILL.md
2	
3	This is a draft for the owner, not yet in the skill. It condenses the wording, symbol, command, menu and shortcut rules of rules.md into what an agent needs while building a screen. Each rule names its rule ids so the reasoning can be looked up.
4	
5	It follows the owner's decisions of 2026-10-23 on every open question (open-questions.md). Two of them shape it most: the app writes every label once in sentence case and kvit-ui gives the macOS title case (Q-3); Windows and Linux get full access keys (Q-11). It assumes the library changes in library-gaps.md steps 1 to 5 exist (`ui.Form`, `Command`, `MenuBar` and the toolbar, Dialog by form); until they do, rules 15 to 20 are things the agent does by hand.
6	
7	The before-and-after pairs come from the survey of kvit-cash, kvit-notes and kvit-works of 2026-10-22 and from kvit-ui's own strings and gallery. The application repositories were not available where this draft was written, so the app pairs are the ones the survey named, with its file:line.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Words, symbols, commands and shortcuts
12	
13	Interface text is not prose. The writing rules for documents and reports ask for whole sentences, spelled-out meaning and no compressed labels; they do not apply to a button, a menu item, a tab or a tooltip. Interface text has its own conventions, shared by Apple and Microsoft: a command starts with its verb, takes one to three words, drops articles, and is named the same everywhere it appears. A sentence on a button is a defect, however clear the sentence is.
14	
15	The rules below hold on every system unless they say "Windows" or "macOS". kvit-ui knows which system it runs on (`ui.Form`; Linux takes the Windows form) and does the platform differences itself where it can: button order, capitalisation, Ctrl or Cmd, the menu bar.
16	
17	### Labels
18	
19	**1. A command is a verb that names what happens.** Buttons and menu items start with a specific verb: Import, Archive, Reconcile, not Manage, Configure or Do it. A statement or a description is not a command. (WRD-1)
20	
21	- "The data is right" (kvit-cash `app/health/card.go:167`) → "Mark correct"
22	- "Rows shown" → "Select all"
23	
24	**2. One to three words.** Use only the words the command needs. When a command seems to need a sentence, the sentence belongs in its Explanation, its dialog, or nowhere. (WRD-2)
25	
26	- "Take the new default" (kvit-cash `app/configuration/editor.go:116`) → "Reset to default…"
27	- "Save to the workspace" (kvit-cash `app/configuration/editor.go:157`) → "Save"
28	- "Move the selected column earlier" (`duallist.go:56`) → "Move up"
29	
30	**3. No articles, no "my" or "your".** Not on labels, menu items, tabs or tooltips. (WRD-3)
31	
32	- "Close the preview" (kvit-cash `app/preview/preview.go:56`) → "Back" (it sits on a back arrow)
33	- "Use the shipped default" (kvit-cash `app/configuration/editor.go:153`) → the same command as rule 2's "Reset to default…"
34	- "Clear the filter" (`searchfield.go:56`) → "Clear"
35	- "Dismiss this notice" (`feedback.go:261`) → "Dismiss"
36	
37	**4. The label says exactly what happens.** Read the handler before naming it. A label that names a different action from the one that runs is the worst kind of wrong. (WRD-1, WRD-10)
38	
39	- "Add the rows shown" that selects every row (kvit-cash `app/transactions/transactions.go:112`) → "Select all"
40	- "Delete…" that moves a folder to the trash (kvit-notes `app/actions.go:108`) → "Move to Trash…" on macOS, "Delete…" with the dialog saying it goes to the Recycle Bin on Windows and Linux
41	
42	**5. Ellipsis when the command asks for more.** A command that opens a dialog, a chooser or a confirmation before acting ends with "…" (one character). One that acts at once has none. On Windows, a command whose whole job is to show a window (Settings, Properties, About) has none. Set `Asks` and let the component add it. (WRD-4)
43	
44	- "Export the ledger" opening a dialog (gallery `dialogMoved`) → "Export…"
45	
46	**6. Write sentence case; kvit-ui does the rest.** Write every label once, in sentence case: "Select all", "Don't save". On macOS the component turns menu items, buttons, tabs and column headings into title case; on Windows and Linux everything stays as written, window and dialog titles included. Never write title case yourself, and never mix the two in one menu. (WRD-6)
47	
48	- kvit-notes File menu (`app/menus.go:39-56`), "Quick Capture…" beside "Quick capture note…" → every item in sentence case
49	
50	**7. Confirming buttons name the action; never Confirm.** The button that carries out a dialog says what it does. A message that only informs has one button: Close on Windows, OK on macOS. OK, Cancel and Apply belong only to a properties dialog of one object (Windows). Yes and No appear only together, on Windows, where no specific answer is possible. The abandoning button is Cancel; once the work is done it becomes Close. Every dialog has a safe button that leaves without acting. (WRD-7, WRD-8)
51	
52	- "OK" on Insert Link (kvit-notes `app/links.go:260`) → "Insert"
53	- "OK" on Confirm import (kvit-notes `app/exchange.go:299`) → "Import"
54	- Dialog's default ConfirmText "Confirm" (`feedback.go:424`) → always set it: "Delete", "Import", "Send"
55	- "Delete them" (gallery `dialogDestructive`) → "Delete"
56	
57	**8. Busy words say what is happening.** Not "Working…", "Loading…" or "Please wait": an -ing phrase naming the operation. (WRD-25)
58	
59	- Button BusyText "Working…" (`button.go:73`) → "Importing statement…"
60	
61	**9. A search field says what it searches.** (CTL-15)
62	
63	- "Filter…" (`searchfield.go:38`) → "Search transactions"
64	
65	**10. Tooltips are short and add something.** A symbol-only button's Label is its tooltip and its screen-reader name: the command, verb first. Explanation adds a sentence only when the name cannot say it: why the control is disabled, what it opens. On Windows kvit-ui adds the shortcut, "Bold (Ctrl+B)". Never repeat a visible label, never explain how to operate the control. (WRD-13, HLP-2)
66	
67	- "Select every row the current filter shows" (`table.go:843`) → "Select shown rows"
68	
69	### Symbols or words
70	
71	**11. A symbol for a familiar action, words for the rest.** Bold, italic, search, delete, close, back, add: symbols, as IconButtons with a Label. An action people would have to guess from a symbol: words. (CMD-22)
72	
73	**12. Never letters or punctuation standing in for a symbol.** A text button reading "B", "<>" or "+ Insert" is a symbol drawn in the wrong component. Use an IconButton with the meaning name and a Label in words. If the symbol you need is not in the catalogue, say so; do not type it. (CMD-22)
74	
75	- "B", "I", "U", "S" (kvit-notes `app/toolbar.go:105-146`, `editor/formatbar.go:59-71`) → IconButtons named "Bold", "Italic", "Underline", "Strikethrough"
76	- "<>" → IconButton named "Code"; "H" → IconButton named "Heading"
77	- "+ Insert" → "Insert…" with the `plus` symbol before the words
78	
79	**13. One symbol, one meaning, across the whole app.** Before using a symbol, check what else in the app uses it. The close symbol closes; it does not archive, withdraw, remove or cancel. (CON-2)
80	
81	- X for archive (kvit-works `ui/shell/overviewcard.go:61`) → `archive`, "Archive"
82	- X for withdraw (kvit-works `ui/conversation/view.go:1242`) → `undo`, "Withdraw"
83	- X labelled "Close agent" that opens a browser (kvit-works `ui/shell/detailheader.go:184`) → `external`, "Open in browser"
84	
85	### Commands
86	
87	**14. One command, one name, everywhere.** A command has the same words in the menu bar, on its button, in its tooltip, in the tray menu and in any dialog it opens. Define it once as a `Command` and make every control from it. (CON-1)
88	
89	- "Quick Capture…" (kvit-notes `app/tray.go:52`), "Quick capture note…" (`app/menus.go:51`), "Quick capture" (`app/capture.go:25`) → one command, "Quick capture…"
90	
91	**15. Every command is in the menu bar.** Buttons, toolbars and context menus are shortcuts to commands that also live in a menu. A command that exists only on a button cannot be found from the keyboard or by a reader who missed the button. (CMD-1)
92	
93	**16. Standard commands in the standard menus.** Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Select all and Find go in Edit; New, Open, Save, Close and Print in File; show and hide commands in View. Settings and About go where the platform puts them: on Windows and Linux, Settings is the last item of the sidebar or the toolbar's More menu and About is a section at the bottom of the Settings page; on macOS both are in the app menu. Exit on Windows, Quit on macOS. On Windows an app with few commands may use a toolbar with a More menu instead of a menu bar; every command must still be on one of them. (CMD-1 to CMD-8)
94	
95	**17. Menus: most used first, grouped, short, destructive last.** Separate groups with separators; at most one level of submenu, none in a context menu on Windows; a destructive item goes last, after a separator. A context menu holds only what applies to what was clicked. (CMD-10, CMD-12, CMD-13, CMD-23)
96	
97	**18. A toggle says what it does.** On macOS a menu item swaps its words ("Show sidebar" / "Hide sidebar"); on Windows it keeps its name and shows a tick. Give MenuItem both words and let it choose. (WRD-12)
98	
99	### Shortcuts
100	
101	**19. Standard commands get the standard shortcut.** If the app has Save, Ctrl+S (Cmd-S) saves; Find, New, Close, Undo, Redo, Copy, Paste, Select all likewise. Use the standard `Command` and the key comes with it. A shortcut that does nothing when its command cannot act stays silent. (KEY-2)
102	
103	- kvit-cash Save with no Ctrl+S → the standard Save command
104	- kvit-works without Ctrl+F, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+W → Find focuses the SearchField; New and Close as standard commands
105	
106	**20. Menus show their shortcuts.** A menu item whose command has a key shows it; that is how people learn it. Context menus on macOS show none. (KEY-14, CMD-11)
107	
108	- kvit-cash: none of 23 menu items shows a shortcut; kvit-notes: 4 of 109 → every item with a key shows it
109	
110	**21. Few new shortcuts, and never the system's.** Give a new shortcut only to a frequent command, on a letter that recalls its name, built on the command modifier (`mod.OSMenuCommand()`, never `mod.Control` or `mod.Command` by hand). Never Alt+letter on Windows (access keys own it), never Ctrl+Alt, never a key the system or another command already uses. (KEY-3, KEY-4, KEY-5)
111	
112	**22. Access keys on Windows and Linux.** Write labels with "&" before the access letter ("&Import"); kvit-ui underlines it on Windows and Linux and drops it on macOS. Not on OK, Cancel, Close, links or tabs. Two controls in one window never share a letter. (KEY-15)
113	
114	### Dialogs and messages
115	
116	**23. kvit-ui orders dialog buttons; do not.** Give Dialog its ConfirmText and CancelText and let it place them: the main action first and the safe button last on Windows and Linux, the default button last on macOS. Never build a row of dialog buttons yourself. (WIN-1)
117	
118	**24. Ask only when it matters.** No dialog before an action that can be undone: do it, and show ConfirmInPlace or a toast with Undo. Ask before a rare action that loses data for good, and then say what will be lost. (MSG-3)
119	
120	**25. A message says what happened and what to do.** The title is the problem or the question, specific, never "Error". The detail adds the cause and the fix. An input error sits under its field and says how to put it right. No "Oops", no blame, and no "we": write "Couldn't save the file", which reads right on both systems. (MSG-4, MSG-5, MSG-6, WRD-28)
121	
122	**26. Explanations stay short.** A setting gets a label and at most one short line. A longer explanation goes behind a Hint. A paragraph that is always on screen is read once and then ignored. (WRD-22)
123	
124	- kvit-notes `app/settings.go:269`, a permanent 50-word paragraph under one setting → one line, the rest in a Hint
125	
126	**27. Settings apply at once.** An app's settings are a page (on macOS a window) where each change takes effect as it is made: no OK, Cancel or Apply. On Windows a setting that applies at once is a switch, not a checkbox. Each setting is one row: its label, a one-line description where needed, and the control. (WIN-16, WIN-23, CTL-2, WRD-22)
127	
128	- A settings dialog with OK and Cancel → a Settings page whose changes apply at once
129	
130	**28. Links go somewhere; buttons act.** A link opens a page, a window or a help topic and commits nothing; anything that changes data is a button. Every link's tooltip says where it leads. Labels end without a colon. (CTL-26, WRD-19)
